patch_description: Crossover of the two best implementations. From the current program (score 0.70) we keep: (a) the fast incremental area updates — moving one point only affects its 66 triangles, so we cache all 286 areas and update only the affected slice; (b) the structured ring/disk initializations (ring of 12 + center, 13-ring, 7+6 double ring, etc.) which are far better baselines than random disks; (c) the greedy sigma-decay descent with restarts. From the second program (score 0.52) we borrow: (a) coordinated moves on the three vertices of the current bottleneck (minimum-area) triangle — these escape local optima that single-point moves cannot; (b) the soft bottleneck objective (mean of the smallest k triangle areas) for occasional uphill acceptance, allowing annealing-like escape from poor basins; (c) the final strict greedy polish phase focused on the bottleneck triangle. The hybrid runs greedy incremental descent (cheap due to caching), injects coordinated bottleneck-triangle moves periodically, and finishes each restart with a strict polish. This should strictly dominate both parents: better objective per unit time (incremental updates ~5x faster evaluation) plus better basin-escape (coordinated + soft moves), all under a deterministic time budget.
